name: St Nicholas' church
name_1343: St Nicholas' (Nicolai kerke), merchants' parish church
confidence: attested hall church (1230s-c.1290) with low west tower, sacristy, north porch (1st half 14th c.), St Barbara chapel (1342); 1343 plan reconstructed inside the surviving site (plausible composite)
period_notes: Rule (maintainer 2026-10-07): features dated after 1343 are left out; where the 1343 state is unrecorded, a slightly simplified form of the later, documented church is used (plausible composite).

Excluded as dated later: the basilica nave and polygonal ambulatory choir (1405-1420 and later), the high tower and its baroque spire, the St Matthew and later side chapels (1470s+), Hermen Rode's high altar (1478-81), the organ, the brass chandeliers.

Attested for 1343: a hall church with nave and two aisles, a square chancel, a sacristy, a low west tower, defensive loopholes in the early fabric, the north porch (first half 14th c.), the St Barbara chapel at the cemetery edge (first recorded 1342), the cemetery.

Unrecorded in 1343, simplified later form: bare grey limestone piers, arches and vault ribs against whitewashed walls and webs (as inside today); grey limestone rubble with buttresses outside and a whitewashed tower with blind arcading under a shingled helm; stone-flag floor with many ledger slabs; single lancets with stained glass; oak benches; candle crowns; a pulpit; a winged retable; side altars funded by merchant families and guilds.
The churchyard is levelled with the church terrace (cemetery and the St Barbara chapel stand on it).

openings.note: north portal under the porch (porch first half 14th c.)

people.role: parish priest at the high altar
merchant at his family's side altar
guild member at the south side altar

program_1343.summary: The wealthy merchant parish of the south-west Lower Town (Westphalian-Gotland founders); side altars of merchant families and guilds; cemetery with the St Barbara charnel chapel.
processes: merchant family devotions at side altars
burials in the church floor and the cemetery
bells from the low west tower
